document: OpenDataRemoval Privacy Platform — n8n Workflow Specification
description: Defines the broker discovery automation workflows — orchestrator/sub-workflow architecture, source fetching, full normalisation, HMAC-authenticated batch posting to the OpenDataRemoval API webhook, error handling, and retry logic.

design_decisions.workflow_structure: One orchestrator workflow triggering sub-workflows per source — failed sources don't block others, each sub-workflow independently testable and enable/disableable
design_decisions.batch_size: 50 brokers per POST — avoids body size limits, gives natural retry unit
design_decisions.source_failure: Retry up to 3 times then continue — transient failures don't stop successful sources. Persistent failures surface dashboard notification.
design_decisions.normalisation: n8n handles full normalisation into OpenDataRemoval broker schema before posting — API webhook receives clean validated data

credentials_needed.name: OpenDataRemoval API Webhook
credentials_needed.note: Cannot be stored as static credential — computed in Code node each request

credentials_needed.name: GitHub HTTP
credentials_needed.note: GitHub raw content URLs are public. Rate limit: 60 req/hour unauthenticated.

n8n_environment.workflow_storage: Persisted in opendataremoval_n8n_data volume. JSON exports committed to workflows/ in repo.

WF-001.name: Broker Discovery — Orchestrator
WF-001.description: Weekly scheduled workflow that triggers all source sub-workflows in sequence. Aggregates results and posts a summary notification to the OpenDataRemoval API.

WF-002.name: Broker Discovery — GitHub Big-Ass List
WF-002.description: Fetches and parses the Big-Ass Data Broker Opt-Out List from GitHub. Handles Markdown format parsing.

WF-003.name: Broker Discovery — EFF Surveillance Self-Defense
WF-003.description: Fetches broker data from EFF-maintained lists. Handles JSON format.
WF-003.note: URL configurable via n8n environment variable — defaults to known EFF resource

WF-004.name: Broker Discovery — Custom URL
WF-004.description: Fetches broker data from a user-configurable URL. Supports JSON and CSV formats. Disabled by default — enable and configure URL in n8n UI.

WF-005.name: Discovery Run Complete — Notify
WF-005.description: Called at end of orchestrator run. Posts a run summary to the OpenDataRemoval API system notification endpoint.
WF-005.trigger: Execute Workflow node (called by WF-001 after all sources complete)

nodes.name: Schedule Trigger
nodes.description: Fires every Sunday at 06:00 in configured timezone

nodes.name: Set Run Context
nodes.description: Initialises run metadata passed to all sub-workflows

nodes.name: Run GitHub Big-Ass List
nodes.description: Trigger WF-002 and wait for completion. On error: catch and continue.
nodes.error_handling: continueOnFail: true — error captured in output

nodes.name: Run EFF List
nodes.description: Trigger WF-003 — runs regardless of WF-002 outcome

nodes.name: Run Custom URL
nodes.description: Trigger WF-004 — only runs if WF-004 is active

nodes.name: Aggregate Results
nodes.description: Collects success/failure/broker counts from all sub-workflow outputs into a single summary object

nodes.name: Fetch README from GitHub
nodes.description: GET raw Markdown from GitHub. Retry 3 times on failure.
nodes.error_handling: On final failure: return { error: true, source_name: github_big_ass_list, message: error.message }

nodes.name: Parse Markdown to Broker List
nodes.description: Extracts broker entries from Markdown table/list format. Returns array of raw broker objects.
nodes.parsing_strategy: Regex scan for lines containing URLs and broker names in table rows or list items
code_logic: Filter lines matching Markdown table row pattern: | BrokerName | URL | Category | ...
For list items: match pattern '- [BrokerName](url)' or '* BrokerName: url'
Extract: name, url, opt_out_url, removal_type (from column/inline text)
Return array of { raw_name, raw_url, raw_opt_out_url, raw_removal_type, raw_category }

nodes.name: Normalise to OpenDataRemoval Schema
nodes.description: Maps raw parsed fields to OpenDataRemoval broker schema fields. Applies category and removal_method mappings.

normalisation_rules.canonical_domain: Extract root domain from raw_url via URL parsing. Lowercase. Remove www. prefix.
normalisation_rules.display_name: Trim whitespace from raw_name. Title-case if ALL CAPS.

category.method: Lowercase raw_category, match against mapping keys via includes()

normalisation_rules.opt_out_url: Use raw_opt_out_url if present. Fallback: raw_url. Validate starts with https://
normalisation_rules.ccpa_applicable: True if category is data_broker or removal_method contains letter/ccpa
normalisation_rules.estimated_response_days: null — not provided by this source

validation: Skip entry if canonical_domain is empty or not a valid domain pattern
Skip entry if canonical_domain is a duplicate within this batch (dedup by domain)

nodes.name: Compute HMAC Signature
nodes.description: Computes HMAC-SHA256 signature of the request body using N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET

nodes.name: POST Batch to Webhook
nodes.description: POST normalised broker batch to OpenDataRemoval API with HMAC signature header

nodes.name: Accumulate Batch Results
nodes.description: Accumulates upserted/skipped/error counts across all batches

WF-003_eff.nodes_summary: Same structure as WF-002 but with JSON parsing instead of Markdown

parsing_strategy.expected_json_shape: Array of objects with name, website, opt_out_url, category fields
parsing_strategy.fallback: If shape differs, attempt field mapping by common key names: url/website/domain, name/broker_name/title
parsing_strategy.on_unrecognised_format: Log warning, return empty broker array, report in summary

WF-003_eff.normalisation: Same rules as WF-002 normalisation node — reuses Code node logic via shared code snippet

format_detection.json: Response Content-Type contains application/json OR body starts with [ or {
format_detection.csv: Response Content-Type contains text/csv OR text/plain AND body contains commas and newlines

csv_parsing.library: n8n built-in CSV parsing via Spreadsheet File node
csv_parsing.header_row: Assumed present. Column names matched case-insensitively.

nodes.name: Compute HMAC
nodes.description: Same HMAC computation as WF-002 n6

config.note: Internal endpoint — authenticated via HMAC, creates system_alert notification in DB

hmac_signing.description: Every POST to /api/webhooks/n8n must include an HMAC-SHA256 signature

n8n_implementation.runtime: Node.js (n8n Code node uses Node.js crypto module)

hmac_signing.api_verification: FastAPI webhook handler: hmac.compare_digest(computed, received) — constant-time comparison

canonical_domain.rule: Extract hostname from URL, remove www. prefix, lowercase

skip_conditions: canonical_domain is a duplicate within current batch
broker_normalisation_rules.ccpa_applicable_heuristic: True if category=data_broker OR removal_method=legal_letter OR source name contains 'ccpa'
broker_normalisation_rules.gdpr_applicable_heuristic: False by default for US-focused discovery sources. Set manually via registry override.

source_fetch_failure.retry_policy: 3 retries with 10s wait between attempts (configured in HTTP Request node)
source_fetch_failure.on_final_failure: Return error summary object to orchestrator: { error: true, source_name, message }
source_fetch_failure.orchestrator_behaviour: Log failure, continue to next source, include failed source in completion notification

webhook_post_failure.retry_policy: 3 retries with 5s wait between attempts per batch
webhook_post_failure.on_final_failure: Log failed batch with broker count, continue to next batch, include in summary
webhook_post_failure.note: Missed brokers will be picked up on the following week's run

parse_error.behaviour: Log error with source URL and raw content snippet. Return empty broker array. Continue workflow.
parse_error.notification: Include parse_error: true in summary returned to orchestrator

hmac_signing_error.behaviour: Stop workflow execution — this is a configuration error. Alert via n8n error workflow.
hmac_signing_error.note: HMAC failure means N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET env var is missing or malformed

workflow_testing.manual_trigger: Each workflow has a Manual Trigger node (disabled in production) that allows one-click test execution from the n8n UI

dry_run_mode.description: Set dry_run=true in Set Run Context node to execute full normalisation without posting to the API
dry_run_mode.implementation: Add IF node after normalisation: if dry_run=true → route to a Set node that logs broker count, else → route to batch/post nodes

workflow_testing.test_webhook_url: Override api_webhook_url in Set Run Context to http://api:8000/api/webhooks/n8n-test for development testing against a mock endpoint

export_process: In n8n UI: Settings → Download → saves workflow as JSON
Place in workflows/ directory with filename matching workflow_id
Commit to git — workflow JSON is the version of record
import_process: In n8n UI: Workflows → Import from File
workflow_versioning.automated_import: Workflows volume mounted read-only at /home/node/.n8n/workflows/ — n8n auto-imports on startup if files present

setup_checklist: 1. Access n8n UI at http://{host}:5678 with N8N_BASIC_AUTH_USER/PASSWORD credentials
2. Verify WEBHOOK_URL environment variable resolves to http://api:8000
3. Verify N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set and matches value in OpenDataRemoval .env
4. Import all 5 workflow JSON files from workflows/ directory
5. Activate WF-001 through WF-005 (WF-004 remains inactive by default)
6. Manually trigger WF-001 once with dry_run=true to verify source connectivity
7. Manually trigger WF-001 once in live mode to seed initial broker registry
8. Verify broker count in OpenDataRemoval dashboard registry view
